response: Causal chain: (1) instruction present -> (2) pre-code extraction produces a numbered requirement list (inherits the parent's front-loaded attention mechanism) -> (3) implementation proceeds with the list as external memory -> (4) the evidence pass forces one concrete artifact per item: an executed check or a specific code location -> (5) items without producible evidence surface as explicit gaps -> (6) gaps get fixed pre-completion -> (7) held-out pass rate rises. The novel link is 4-5: unlike the parent's 'verify each item', which can be satisfied by silent assent, producing evidence has a cost asymmetry — writing a false evidence line requires active confabulation rather than passive skipping, and small models skip more readily than they confabulate under neutral incentives. Fragile links: confabulation under completion pressure (citing a plausible-looking code location without checking it), and evidence-quality collapse (items evidenced by 'implemented in solution()' — technically compliant, discriminating nothing). Supporting evidence needed: positive paired delta; transcripts whose evidence lines reference executed checks (strong) versus bare code citations (weak) in proportions that track per-trial outcomes; candidate failures whose grader-failed clause had a missing or weak evidence line (mechanism-consistent failure). Disconfirming: complete, strong evidence lines on trials that still fail their grader clause — that would locate the failure in extraction fidelity or algorithmic inability, outside this arm's reach.
